Irish Steelworkers Walk Out, Forcing Production Halts Across Major Plants

A nationwide walkout by steel industry workers has brought production to a standstill at Ireland’s largest steel manufacturing sites, leaving employers and unions at an impasse as the industrial action enters its third day.

The strike, organised by the United Steelworkers of Ireland (USI), began Monday morning after weekend negotiations with the Irish Steel Producers’ Association (ISPA) failed to resolve a dispute over pay and working conditions. More than 2,100 workers, including operators, maintenance staff, and support personnel, have walked off the job at all three of the country’s main steel plants: Emerald Steel in County Louth, Atlantic Bar & Plate in Cork, and Shannon Steelworks in Limerick.

“Steelworkers are sending a clear message that years of pay restraint and understaffed shifts are no longer acceptable,” said USI General Secretary Fiona McCabe, addressing workers gathered outside the Emerald Steel gates on Tuesday. “Our members want a fair share in the success of this vital industry.”

All blast furnaces, rolling mills, and processing lines at the affected sites remain idle. ISPA spokesperson Michael O’Donoghue confirmed that no steel has been produced or shipped since the strike began. “The shutdown is complete. We are urgently seeking engagement with the union to restore operations and safeguard the future of Irish steel.”

Industry analysts estimate that the sector is losing roughly 4,500 tonnes of output per day as a result of the stoppage. According to ISPA, the three plants together account for over 95% of Ireland’s annual crude steel production.

With no sign of a breakthrough, management at the affected companies have begun contingency planning, but have so far refrained from bringing in temporary replacements. “We are committed to constructive dialogue and hope to reach a resolution that recognises the contribution of our workforce,” said an Emerald Steel representative.

As pickets continue outside the shuttered plants, both sides have called for urgent third-party mediation. Talks are scheduled to resume later this week, but steel production across Ireland remains at a standstill for now.
